newsitem.title: SLOVAKIA: Slovak trade gap widens more slowly in June.
newsitem.headline: Slovak trade gap widens more slowly in June.

text.p: Slovakia's trade deficit widened in the first half of the year to 32.57 billion crowns ($937 million) from 26.98 billion a year earlier but the growth in the deficit slowed, the Statistical Bureau said (SUSR) said on Wednesday.
Imports totalled 177.33 billion crowns in the half, a year-on-year increase of 12.6 percent, while exports rose 12.9 percent to 144.76 billion crowns.
The bureau revised Slovakia's January-May trade deficit to 29.62 billion crowns from 29.86 billion. No explanation of the revision was immediately available.
The trade gap for June alone was 2.95 billion crowns, compared with 4.21 billion in May and 1.34 billion in June 1996.
The fastest rise in imports in the first half was in audio and video equipment, which jumped 58 percent year-on-year to 16.07 billion crowns.
Fossil fuels and mineral oils accounted for the largest share of imported goods, totalling 31.22 billion crowns and showing a 17.9 percent year-on-year increase.

Technology imports, such as equipment for upgrading the ageing Jaslovske Bohunice nuclear power plant and the completion of the Mochovce nuclear plant, totalled 28.29 billion crowns, up 20.2 percent year-on-year.
The fastest increase in exports was in cars, tractors and accessories which were together worth 16.39 billion crowns -- a 94.3 percent rise from the first half of 1996.
The main export items included steel and iron which totalled 19.649 billion crowns and were up 3.9 percent year-on-year.
The Czech Republic remains Slovakia's main trading partner, accounting for 27.7 percent of exports and 23.5 percent of its imports.
Russia and Germany both accounted for 15.4 percent of Slovak imports, followed by Italy with 5.5 percent.
Other key Slovak export partners were Germany, accounting for 23.2 percent, and Austria with 6.5 percent.
Slovakia's trade deficit with OECD countries totalled 8.934 billion crowns in the first half of 1997, while the trade gap with EU states totalled 4.577 billion crowns.
